mechanism: Sparse, accuracy-only benchmarking leaves model limitations invisible because evaluators never observe metrics they do not measure. HELM's causal structure: (1) taxonomize scenarios × metrics into a cross-product space, (2) enforce dense, standardized measurement of 7 metrics across all 30 models and 16 core scenarios, (3) expose trade-offs that were structurally absent when models shared no common evaluation scenarios. Coverage breadth causally determines what failure modes the community can detect.
invariant: Expanding evaluation from single-metric to multi-metric measurement across a standardized scenario set will surface trade-offs between accuracy and other desiderata (robustness, fairness, calibration, toxicity, efficiency) that single-metric benchmarks structurally cannot detect, regardless of the specific models or domain.
prediction: Models ranked highest on accuracy-only benchmarks will show meaningfully different relative rankings when fairness, toxicity, or calibration metrics are included, with some top-accuracy models dropping significantly in holistic ranking—falsifiable by computing rank-order correlations between accuracy-only and multi-metric composite rankings.
failure_mode: If all 7 measured metrics are strongly positively correlated across models (i.e., high-accuracy models uniformly also score best on fairness, calibration, toxicity, etc.), the multi-metric structure adds no discriminative signal, and the mechanism's core claim—that holistic coverage reveals hidden trade-offs—fails empirically.
source_excerpt: Prior to HELM, models on average were evaluated on just 17.9% of the core HELM scenarios, with some prominent models not sharing a single scenario in common. We improve this to 96.0%: now all 30 models have been densely benchmarked on a set of core scenarios and metrics under standardized conditions.
